Draw the File Surface — sitting 1

These are wireframes drawn at the app's real sizes and colours: the 640 column, the 28 margin, the 8 grid, 15/12/20 type, 36 controls, the dark palette and the shipped fonts. They are not builds. Each drawing below that can go more than one way has a selector above it, and the questions at the bottom send your answers back. Two things need the real renderer rather than a browser, and I'll build those once you've chosen: how Persian orders inside egui (the browser's bidi is better than ours, so a wireframe can't show the bug) and the four-digit counts on screen.

Words used on this page

preview
the screen an import shows before anything is written: what the file will do to your collection (ADR-0022 §3)
gate
the Import / Cancel pair at the bottom of the preview. Nothing is written until Import is pressed
header
what the file says about itself (author, description, licence). It's a stranger's text, kept apart from the effects (§7)
effects
the lines saying what will happen: new notes, notes moving in, notes deleted, a rename, a deck left empty
reach line
the line 165px above the bottom of the window where the last control sits, measured by thumb (ADR-0035)
primary
the one filled control on a screen that has no card, which is the way forward (ADR-0034 §2)
text action
an unframed alternative sitting beside a primary, like Cancel (ADR-0034 §5)
row
the list band the note list uses: text, a small caption under it, and the whole band opens the file (ADR-0039)

How I sorted the questions

  • decidedalready settled by an ADR. I'm drawing it, not asking you. Listed at the end so you can object.
  • defectwrong today with an obvious fix, so I'll just fix it. Also listed at the end.
  • yourssix questions. Each has a drawing, my recommendation, and a form at the bottom.

1 · The preview, on the update path

The French A1 file against fixture decks: the state the ticket says to judge this screen on. The before is at the end of this section.

Q1 · the header:
  1. The heading is the file's name as it arrived, the object you opened. A share with no name reads A deck file.
  2. The header (by, licence, description) sits between the heading and a hairline, apart from the effects. It's plain text, so a stranger's **bold** would show as asterisks.
  3. Each deck is its name on its own line in the bold face, with the path (updating a deck you already have) as a caption under it. The two are no longer one joined string, which is what reversed them in Persian. The effects are indented one step under their deck.
  4. Destructive lines get no colour, as ADR-0016 §6 requires: facts only, no verb, no colour. Your review history is untouched. always closes the list.
  5. The gate is pinned outside the scroll, with its bottom edge on the reach line (ADR-0039 §8). Import is the primary. Cancel is a text action beside it.
Before: the specimen today

2 · Three decks, one of them Persian

The file فارسی and 2 more.cdeck. Today the deck line comes out as "updating a deck you already have — فارسی" because the name and the words were joined into one string. Splitting them is the defect fix. What remains to decide is which edge a right-to-left name sits on once it's on its own line.

Q2 · a Persian name:
  1. A applies the note-list rule (ADR-0039 §4 and ADR-0040 §6: content, not furniture). The name and its caption mirror, like a row and its caption. The effects are the app's own English, so they stay left.
  2. B keeps every deck name on the left and isolates it, so it can't reorder the words around it but doesn't move either.
  3. Either way, a name inside a sentence (moving in from X, renaming your X) is an isolated run. The build has to prove that in egui. The browser does it for free, which is why this can't be judged from the wireframe alone.
Before: the specimen today

3 · The file list, as a block on Settings

Where it lives was settled by The File Surface. Where the block sits on Settings belongs to Take the Settings Slice, so the controls above it are faded out. Each file is a note-list row: the band opens its preview, and there are no actions because the file seam has no delete.

Q3 · the icon test:
  1. The caption comes from the file's manifest, as ADR-0022 §11 draws it: deck · 18 notes · 3 retractions, and for an archive its date and counts. It's still no payload inflated. Today it says only deck, and I'm counting that as a defect.
  2. The name is the row's text and the description is its caption: two elements. That alone fixes "and 2 more.cdeck — deck فارسی". The Persian-named row aligns right, like a Persian note in the note list.
  3. Why this is the icon rule's third test: delete and move already had pictures everyone knows, so repetition only had to attach them to a place. Deck, collection archive and unreadable don't. They're like Suspend. If words win here, the sentence in ADR-0039 becomes the rule: a picture only where the symbol already exists.
  4. The list reads itself when Settings opens. The List the files button was a development control.

4 · Nothing will change, and a refusal

Re-opening a file you've already imported is the second most likely import there is (§4). A refusal replaces the preview completely: one plain sentence, and no detail that invites someone to repair the file.

Q4 · the no-change gate: Show:
  1. ADR-0022 says the no-op "costs one dismissal". An Import that writes nothing is a button whose only effect is to leave the screen, which is what Close already does.
  2. A refusal has one way out, so it's a primary on its own. After a cold start, Close lands on the count picker (§6).

Your six questions

Pick an answer and press Queue. You can change it until you send. Anything you'd like to say about a drawing, annotate it directly.

Q1 · How is the file's own header set apart from the effects? (section 1)
Q2 · Once a Persian deck name has its own line, which edge does it sit on? (section 2)
Q3 · The icon rule's third test: does a file row get a picture? (section 3)
Q4 · When nothing will change, what does the gate offer? (section 4)
Q5 · The words on the file-list block (section 3)

They must say what the list is, never what's missing (ADR-0024 §3). There's no export screen yet, so the empty state can't point to one.

Q6 · A finding, not a drawing: restore has no screen anywhere

The list shows .ccoll archives (ADR-0022 §11 even gives them a date so you can tell them apart), and cairn-export already has restore_preview and the store has ingest. But nothing in the app reads an archive, so opening one from the list reaches the deck refusal "This is a collection archive, not a deck file." The app also never writes an archive: only the bench does.

Settled already, or a defect I'll just fix

decided

  • The list is a block on Settings. The preview takes the screen and has no nav entry (The File Surface, ADR-0022 §9).
  • Which lines appear and in what order, the wording rules, and absent, never zero (§3).
  • The header is plain text, length-bounded and drawn through bidi::job (§7).
  • No colour on destructive lines (ADR-0016 §6's form, cited by §3).
  • The row is controls::row, and its band opens the file (ADR-0039 §1).
  • Import is the primary, Cancel a text action beside it (ADR-0034 §2, §5).
  • The gate is pinned outside the scroll on the reach line (ADR-0039 §8).
  • After Import, the app goes to the note list, filtered to the deck when there's one (§5). Nothing is reported afterwards.

defect

  • Name and statement joined into one string, in the row and the deck line, so bidi reorders them.
  • A name inside a sentence isn't an isolated run.
  • Counts aren't grouped (1202, not 1,202), and 6 new is missing its noun.
  • Row caption says only the profile, not the manifest's counts (§11).
  • Lower-case renaming your…, and quoted names where the deck name alone reads.
  • The development words (Arrived, Sniffed, Name it gave) and the two specimen blocks go away.
